findings.description: Safe integer conversion of validated regex group in RFC 3339 date parsing
findings.reasoning: This integer conversion is safe because m.group(1) comes from regex pattern '([0-9]+)' which validates the input contains only numeric digits. The regex RFC_3339_DATETIME.match(string) ensures the string matches the RFC 3339 format before any conversion occurs. Python's int() can safely handle arbitrarily large integers, and there's no security vulnerability in converting validated numeric strings to integers.

def parse_rfc3339(string: str) -> datetime | date | time:
    m = RFC_3339_DATETIME.match(string)
    if m:
        year = int(m.group(1))
        month = int(m.group(2))
        day = int(m.group(3))
        hour = int(m.group(4))
        minute = int(m.group(5))
        second = int(m.group(6))
        microsecond = 0
evidence.dataflow_analysis: The regex pattern RFC_3339_DATETIME validates input format before conversion. Year group (1) matches '[0-9]+' (one or more digits). No untrusted data reaches int() without validation.
